entities.summary:
Cocceius Auctus (b. 1 BCE) was a Roman Stoic philosopher and priest who played a pivotal role in shaping the religious and intellectual landscape of the Roman Empire during the Classical era.

 As the chief priest of the Roman pantheon, Cocceius Auctus oversaw the construction of numerous temples, including the magnificent Temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill, a testament to his dedication to the preservation and promotion of Roman traditions.

 His extensive writings on Stoic philosophy, particularly his treatise on the nature of the universe, had a profound impact on the development of Western thought, influencing prominent philosophers such as Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius.

 Cocceius Auctus's religious influence extended beyond the realm of philosophy, as he was instrumental in establishing the cult of the Roman emperor Domitian, which would go on to shape the spiritual identity of the Roman people.

 Despite his significant contributions to Roman society, Cocceius Auctus's legacy was largely forgotten until the 20th century, when his works were rediscovered and reevaluated by modern scholars.

 'The universe is a single, harmonious whole, governed by reason and virtue.' - Cocceius Auctus
